On-site rule rulings and result record verification are connected: the former applies the rules based on observation, and the latter checks timing, scoring, and records. The six steps below are an editorial summary; the actual division of work and procedures follow the event rules.
On-site rule rulings
Learn the rules → check the venue → confirm the division of work → observe the contest → communicate the ruling → record and report
Grounded rulings, signals, and event records
Result record verification
Verify the scoring method → receive the original sheet → recalculate the results → compare the entries → verify corrections → report the results
Traceable records of results and discrepancy checks
Shared occupational foundation
Sport rules · factual observation · accurate records · teamwork · neutrality · qualifications and authorization
How do rule rulings and result verification differ?

On-site rulings focus on observation and applying the rules; result verification focuses on consistency between the original records, the calculation, and the entries. Some events have one person doing both and some split them across an officiating team, and these two lines are not treated as uniform national job titles.

Judge observed behavior under the applicable competition rules and apply the corresponding penalty or event control.
Check timing, scoring, and calculation records so that reported results match the original basis.

The work requires continuously verifying rules, observing facts, comparing records, and handling disagreements. The six questions below are an editorial self-check; when real rulings or qualifications are involved, first verify under the actual sport and event procedure.

Explain the decision using the same applicable rules and observed facts, hear the objection clearly, and record or escalate it under the event procedure; the standard must not change because of loudness, personal acquaintance, or preference.

This page reviews the 150 yuan per person per day officiating fee at the 2025 Baoji youth event and the absence of a dedicated officiating labor allowance for the 2026 Yangcheng triathlon training practice. The two are historical conditions from different places, dates, and statuses, and do not constitute a national wage sample or a promise of current openings.

The Yangcheng training application and the course running September 3–6 have both passed, and the absence of a dedicated allowance for the practice does not represent future event pay or that officials across China are unpaid.

description.text: Officials, referees, and other sports officials observe contests in sports competitions, identify rule violations, decide penalties or scores, check the venue and equipment, and verify timing results. Here, refereeing and officiating refer to sports competition functions, not legal arbitration or administrative posts. Judging fit requires looking at mastery of the rules, accuracy of observation, communication under pressure, neutrality, and record-keeping ability; the specific qualifications, appointment, and work rhythm vary with the sport and event.
